topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising within a susceptible cell and a permissive environment can drive cancer evolution.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the role of chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and uncertainty surrounding how much environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than cancer being simply bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma developing the argument through a detailed example.

topics.label: How environmental carcinogens damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular processes through which environmental exposures produce DNA damage capable of generating cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent promotion for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Biological context and carcinogen susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility to carcinogens depends on biological context and consolidate the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Tracing exposure through mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how mutation patterns in cancer genomes can provide evidence of exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods for assessing carcinogenicity and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic potential can be investigated when direct experimental exposure of humans is unacceptable.

topics.label: Concluding summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
